texture_family: hand-layered paper grain with fibrous cut edges
palette_summary: warm orchard greens, muted amber sunlight, cream paper layers, soft slate blues for fatigue states, restrained honey highlights for brain and body signals
line_treatment: clean cut-paper silhouettes with fine hand-drawn anatomical and diagram lines
lighting: soft early morning orchard daylight with gentle amber highlights and cooler fatigue shadows
frame_language: a recurring layered paper illustration window mounted on a softly textured botanical card; irregular cut-paper edges, shallow overlapping layers, and a consistent inner scene panel that feels like a handcrafted educational field journal page
subtitle_reserve: a calm lower paper layer occupying approximately the bottom 14–18% of the 9:16 frame; use simple orchard texture, soft ground shadows, or empty paper grain while keeping faces, hands, baskets, diagrams, and key objects away from this area
subject_constraints: allowed vocabulary includes orchard tools, harvest baskets, garden and farm environments, storybook human figures, paper anatomical overlays, memory and attention diagrams, simple body-system illustrations; avoid modern screens, futuristic interfaces, or clinical realism
hero_rendering_in_world: protagonist keeps the recognizable hair silhouette, beard, and overalls silhouette, translated into layered paper-cut shapes with warm fabric textures and simplified facial details matching the handcrafted world
negative_constraints: no photorealism, no 3D CGI, no anime, no glossy digital painting, no hyper-real anatomy, no beat-by-beat style changes
reason: A new style is required by the operator directive. The paper-cut educational storybook approach fits the orchard setting and sleep topic by making everyday fatigue effects visually approachable while allowing anatomical accents for memory, immune, blood sugar, and brain explanations. Recent styles already include layered anatomical storybook paper and multiple manuscript/fresco approaches, so this avoids repeating the same texture family while preserving the project's handcrafted documentary feel.
